strings.title: The First-Class Carriage
strings.hint: Who can enter a locked compartment without forcing it or attracting attention? Then ask: who paid the price when Al-Ufuq collapsed twenty years ago?
strings.solvedText:
Culprit: carriage attendant Salim Waked.

He was the son of Al-Ufuq's chief accountant. Twenty years ago, the victim deliberately bankrupted the company to buy it for next to nothing. Salim's father died in debt, accused of forgery he had never committed. Salim tracked the victim for years until he became the attendant on his favorite carriage. On the chosen night, he entered with the service key, served the usual midnight coffee laced with poison, washed the cup, and locked the door again.

What convicted him: the only service key used that hour, a freshly washed cup in a locked kitchen, and his father's old letter in his locker: 'Forgive, my son... but do not forget.'
strings.summary.text: On a northbound night train, businessman Adel Qabbani was found dead in his locked first-class compartment. The train had not stopped all night. A single corridor camera showed that nobody had entered... among the passengers. Only four people had ties to the carriage: his business partner traveling with him, a mysterious lawyer traveling under an alias, and the carriage attendant whose face everyone recognized but nobody noticed.
strings.summary.victim.name: Adel Qabbani
strings.summary.timeline[0].l: Last seen alive by the attendant
strings.summary.timeline[2].l: His partner knocks without an answer
strings.scene.intro: A compartment secured from inside with a safety chain... which can be moved from outside with a service key. No struggle: the poison in the coffee worked quietly. The coffee cup vanished from the compartment and turned up washed in a locked kitchen.
strings.scene.notes[0]: The safety chain can be opened from outside with a service key
strings.scene.notes[1]: A washed coffee cup in a kitchen locked at midnight
strings.scene.notes[2]: The corridor camera recorded no passenger entering
strings.scene.notes[3]: The victim ordered his usual coffee from the attendant at 23:45
strings.evidence[0].title: Service Key
strings.evidence[0].desc: The only key used between 23:30 and 01:00, according to the door sensor — held exclusively by the attendant.
strings.evidence[1].title: The Washed Cup
strings.evidence[1].desc: Washed after the kitchen officially closed; traces of a hurried rinse and a drop of coffee remain beneath the base.
strings.evidence[2].title: An Old Letter
strings.evidence[2].desc: A letter from the attendant's father before his death, describing the injustice at Al-Ufuq: 'Forgive, my son... but do not forget.'
strings.evidence[3].title: The New Acquisition Agreement
strings.evidence[3].desc: A deal giving the partner control if the victim is absent — a ready-made motive on paper.
strings.evidence[4].title: The Ticket Under an Alias
strings.evidence[4].desc: The lawyer traveled under an alias, her bag full of old case files against the victim.
strings.evidence[5].title: Coffee Analysis
strings.evidence[5].desc: The communal flask was uncontaminated — the poison was added specifically to the cup.
strings.suspects[0].name: Fares Dabbas
strings.suspects[0].relation: Traveling with him to sign a deal
strings.suspects[0].alibi: 'I was in my compartment reviewing the agreement. I knocked on his door at two in the morning because I was worried.'
strings.suspects[0].statement: The deal gives me control if he is absent — true, and the paperwork makes me look guilty. But who kills his partner on a train where they are almost alone together? If I wanted to commit murder, I would choose a crowded city, not a moving sardine tin.
strings.suspects[1].name: Salim Waked
strings.suspects[1].relation: Has worked the northern route for 6 years
strings.suspects[1].alibi: 'I served his usual coffee, then stayed in the service compartment until dawn.'
strings.suspects[1].statement: Mr. Qabbani was a regular passenger and a generous tipper. I knew his order by heart: black coffee with a touch of cardamom, at midnight precisely. I served it and left. The kitchen? My colleague locked it, and I do not have its key... I think.
strings.suspects[2].name: The lawyer 'N. S.'
strings.suspects[2].relation: Traveled near him under an alias
strings.suspects[2].alibi: 'I boarded in disguise because I was compiling a case against him — pursuing him through the law, not physically.'
strings.suspects[2].statement: I represent twenty families ruined by his acquisitions and was documenting his trip for a major lawsuit. The alias was a professional precaution. His death is my greatest loss: the case dies with the defendant.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Second-carriage attendant
strings.witnesses[0].statement: I locked the kitchen myself at midnight... but its spare key hangs in the first carriage's service compartment — with Salim.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Passenger in compartment 4
strings.witnesses[1].statement: Around one, I heard water running for a long time from the direction of the kitchen. It struck me as strange because the kitchen closes at night.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Train driver
strings.witnesses[2].statement: Door sensors do not lie: no external door opened all night. The killer slept among us until morning.
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Arrival Station Report
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body: Station police were notified of a passenger's death in compartment 3. Passengers in the first carriage were prevented from disembarking.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Toxicology report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body: A slow-acting poison in a single serving of coffee; death occurred during sleep within two hours of consumption.
strings.folders[1].docs[1].title: Chain and Door Report
strings.folders[1].docs[1].body: The safety chain was reattached from outside using a service tool — a technique known only to carriage staff.
strings.folders[2].name: Interviews
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Partner Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body: Nervous, but his account matches his door sensor, which recorded only two documented openings.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Attendant Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body: He denied knowing about the spare kitchen key. It was then found in his uniform jacket pocket.
strings.folders[2].docs[2].title: Lawyer Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[2].body: She disclosed her identity and case file. Her door sensor recorded no opening between 23:00 and 06:00.
strings.folders[3].name: Records
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Door Sensor Log
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body: The only corridor activity between 23:30 and 01:00 involved the service key: compartment 3 opened at 00:04 and the kitchen at 00:19.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: The Old Al-Ufuq File
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body: A bankruptcy engineered 20 years ago. The chief accountant, Waked senior, was blamed for the forgery and died before being cleared. His only son: Salim.
strings.folders[4].name: Confidential files
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: Confession in Compartment 7
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: Confronted with his father's letter and the sensor log, Salim said: 'For twenty years I have served him coffee with a smile... tonight, for the first time, my father drank it with him.'
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Dose Report
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body: The poison came from an industrial pesticide in his father's old storeroom. Salim had kept it all these years.
strings.reports[0].title: The Moving Locked Room Report
strings.reports[0].author: Investigation team
strings.reports[0].body: Nobody entered from outside, and no passenger entered. That left those who are 'unseen because they are always seen': the crew. The service key traced the entire crime.
strings.reports[1].title: A Motive Across the Years
strings.reports[1].author: Assigned investigator
strings.reports[1].body: A crime of long patience: he joined the route 6 years ago to get close to his victim. Planned revenge is more dangerous than passing anger.
strings.notes[0].text: The killer did not break in... he had the right to enter
strings.notes[1].text: Who washed the cup in a locked kitchen?
